note: Site features we are building, considering or blocked on. Planned items are intentions, not promises, and carry no dates. Shipped items were available before this release and cite tests that run on every build.

items.title: Source-linked episode index
items.summary: Every published claim traces to a source cited inside its own record: positions, intensity, police and state response, cities, endings and outcomes.

evidence.label: Claims must cite their own record's sources

items.acceptance: 84 episodes in 81 countries and territories; every position, intensity, state response, city, ending and outcome cites an event-local source; validators pass; checked on the deployed site on 2 Oct 2026 (Pages run 37067775278).

items.title: World map with a complete 249-entry directory
items.summary: An Equal Earth world map coloured by published coverage only, with an A–Z directory of all 249 countries and territories as the complete alternative to the map.

evidence.ref: tests/test_explorer.mjs::map totals agree with reported data
evidence.label: Map totals equal published records
All 249 entries screened without coverage claims

items.acceptance: The map colours published coverage only; every directory entry is selectable; a map failure leaves the list usable.

items.title: Filters, shareable links and CSV export
items.summary: Readers and researchers can reproduce a view: nine filters are kept in the link, and the CSV keeps source URLs.

evidence.ref: tests/test_explorer.mjs::CSV preserves attribution, quoted text, and guards formula injection
evidence.label: CSV keeps sources and escapes formulas

items.acceptance: Permalinks restore 9 filters; CSV keeps source URLs, the recorded-status note and formula escaping.

items.title: 72-hour status ageing
items.summary: Old reports cannot stay 'Reported ongoing': the label lapses 72 hours after the latest evidence.

evidence.label: A rebuild never refreshes an observation

items.acceptance: 'Reported ongoing' becomes 'Needs review' at exactly 72 hours from the latest evidence; re-reading a source never extends it (tested boundary).

items.title: Sourced endings and outcomes
items.summary: What changed, and for whom, without claiming that the protest caused it.

evidence.ref: tests/test_explorer.mjs::outcome view preserves inference, source links and unknown end
evidence.label: Outcome wording keeps inference and causation caveats

items.acceptance: 18 sourced ended or suspended episodes; 57 episodes with documented outcomes, labelled 'Assessment / inference' where inferred, with causation caveats.

items.title: Country search ledger
items.summary: Shows where we looked, not only what we found: a first search is logged for every one of 249 countries and territories.

evidence.label: Failed searches are not zero results

items.acceptance: 249 first searches logged; 'searched' is never shown as 'reviewed' or as 'no protests'.

items.title: Mobile-first redesign
items.summary: A phone-first rebuild: reports, map, Ahead, countries and About as separate views, readable record cards and a full-height record sheet.
items.acceptance: At 390×844 the disclosure and first record are in the first viewport; controls are at least 44 px; no map scroll trap; the record sheet closes reliably; no horizontal scroll at 320 px. Shipped only after the deployed build passes these checks.

items.title: Clear dates and stale warnings
items.summary: Separate, labelled times for the snapshot, the newest evidence, source re-reads, the announced-actions list and the site build, with warnings as the newest evidence ages.
items.acceptance: Every stamp names its subject; stale warnings at 72 hours and 7 days from the newest evidence, recomputed every minute; a missing build stamp shows a note, not an error.

items.title: Cards show stance, intensity, state response, timeframe and source
items.summary: The questions readers ask most are answered on each card instead of deep inside the record.
items.acceptance: Every card shows these rows; positions show their targets; 'not established' is never shown as zero or blank; each card shows publisher, publication date, link and 'AI-assisted check'.

items.title: Ahead page: announced actions and this roadmap
items.summary: One place for what comes next: protest actions that organisations have announced, kept separate from plans for this website. The announcement list itself is blocked (see 'List announced protest actions').
items.acceptance: The empty state explains why it is empty; upcoming.json is validated in the build; tests cover date-passed, postponed and cancelled items; no times, routes or meeting points.

items.title: Add reports after 2 Oct 2026
items.summary: Without fresh reporting nothing in this atlas can be current.
items.blocked_by: The research environment cannot open news websites: the 2 Oct 2026 search logged results but no article could be opened. Needs a fetch-capable connector or a network allowlist for news domains.
items.acceptance: Each new record cites an article that was opened and read, with an access time; the research window advances only for days actually searched; newest evidence is under 72 hours old at publication.

items.title: List announced protest actions
items.summary: Readers asked what is planned next. An announcement is listed only after the announcing article is opened and read.
items.blocked_by: Blocked for the same reason as new reports: no announcing article can be opened from the research environment.
items.acceptance: Each item is read from its source; city and day level only; the announcer is an organisation or institution; it passes validate_upcoming; date-passed handling verified.

items.title: Human editorial review
items.summary: AI-assisted checks are not independent verification. Until a person checks records, the pilot label stays on every page.
items.blocked_by: No human editor or backup has been appointed.
items.acceptance: A named editor and backup; sampled records signed off; one real correction completed end to end; only then may the disclosure change.

items.title: Keep records current within 72 hours
items.summary: A tracker has to keep up with events, and this one cannot yet.
items.blocked_by: Needs new reports and a human editor; both are blocked.
items.acceptance: Newest evidence under 72 hours old on 30 consecutive days, published as a metric; expiring records checked daily.

items.title: Local-language coverage
items.summary: 123 of 128 cited sources are in English, so coverage of many places is thin.
items.blocked_by: Needs fetch access to news websites and language reviewers.
items.acceptance: Per-country language and review windows in the coverage ledger; sensitive translated claims checked by a person.

items.title: Structured police and state response types
items.summary: Free text cannot be filtered safely, and keyword guesses misfile entries. Each response would be coded with a controlled vocabulary in the Mass Mobilization Project style (CC0, cited).
items.acceptance: Fields for acting body, announced or observed, alleged or officially stated, and date; all 37 entries coded from a re-read source; 'not recorded' stays distinct; filter chips only from coded data.

items.title: Turnout ranges with who estimated them
items.summary: Size is asked for, but no number is recorded today.
items.acceptance: Low and high figures with the estimator (organisers, police, officials, media) and method; competing estimates side by side, never averaged; vague words stay text; 'not established' stays distinct.

items.title: Issue tags normalised
items.summary: 66 tags, 36 used once; Labor, Labour and Labour rights split the issue filter.
items.acceptance: A controlled list of about 15 to 20 groups with the original tag kept; old links still resolve; CSV keeps the original tag; the list is ordered alphabetically, not by count.

items.title: Position roles recorded in data
items.summary: Cards cannot honestly say 'government response' without a field for it.
items.acceptance: All 92 positions coded as demonstrators, counter-demonstrators or institutional response from stored records; the pro-Yoon rallies marked as a counter-demonstration; still no tallies.

items.title: Research window beyond 2 Oct 2026
items.summary: The validators already accept a later research window end, and the year filter already follows the data. The merge script still writes a fixed 2 Oct 2026 window end, in the data files and in the coverage note.

evidence.label: Merge script with the fixed window end

items.acceptance: The merge script takes the window end from the days actually searched, and the coverage note is built from it; the window end never advances for a day that was not searched; tests updated.

items.title: Added and corrected dates, with a public corrections log
items.summary: Readers need to know what changed and when; any feed depends on this.
items.acceptance: Per-record added and corrected dates validated; a corrections page lists ID, date, field and reason; an empty log says 'No corrections published yet'.

items.title: Automated accessibility, link and deploy checks
items.summary: Protect the redesign from regressions with checks that run on every pull request. Already built in this release and awaiting deploy evidence: Node 24 action pins, a deploy that newer pushes cannot cancel, and a post-deploy build-stamp check.

evidence.label: Pages workflow with the verify job

items.acceptance: axe or pa11y at 320 and 390 px; internal link check on pull requests; Lighthouse accessibility at least 0.95.

items.title: Episode grouping and movement links
items.summary: Related episodes and counter-demonstrations should connect, but only where a source documents the link.
items.acceptance: Links only where a source documents the relationship; no inferred continuity.

items.title: RSS/Atom feed and notifications
items.summary: For return visits, a feed of records published or corrected in the atlas. Never announced actions.
items.acceptance: Items show both the evidence date and the atlas date. No push alerts until moderation capacity and a demonstrated need exist.

items.title: Versioned snapshots and archive
items.summary: Readers should be able to cite a fixed snapshot.
items.acceptance: Each release snapshot is immutable and dated; comparisons only where coverage is comparable.

items.title: Shareable per-record pages
items.summary: Sharing and search engines need a page per record.
items.acceptance: Each page carries the disclosure and all dates; preview text never implies that reporting is current or continuous.

items.title: Date-range filter and episode timeline view
items.summary: Exploring timeframes beyond the 7- and 30-day options.
items.acceptance: Marks only at dated entries; no filled spans between them.

items.title: Lighter map download
items.summary: Load only the D3 modules the map uses: about 50 KB less to download on the Map view.
items.acceptance: Map add-on under 105 KB gzip with identical rendering; vendored modules licensed and pinned.

items.title: Typo-tolerant search
items.summary: Search that forgives misspellings, once the atlas holds more than about 500 records.
items.acceptance: Typo-tolerant matching with unchanged ordering rules; under 20 KB gzip added; existing search tests still pass.

items.title: Weekly check of cited source links
items.summary: Find cited articles that have moved or disappeared, without blocking publication.
items.acceptance: A weekly non-blocking job reports broken source links; records are never changed automatically.

items.title: Lighter first load before new features
items.summary: The critical script budget had about 600 bytes of room. Ahead, Countries and About now load when first opened, and the build strips comments from stylesheets, so new features fit without raising any ceiling.
items.acceptance: Critical JS at least 15 KB under its ceiling after the split and CSS at least 4 KB under; ceilings unchanged; the modulepreload set equals the 20-module static graph; loading and failure states for the three views are tested.

items.title: Shading by date of newest evidence (opt-in)
items.summary: An optional map shading that follows the newest cited evidence per country, in one hue, off by default, legended, and never a measure of how many protests there were, how large or how severe, or whether anything continues.
items.acceptance: Default map identical to coverage-only; control and legend copy per the 4.1 editorial deck; the ramp passes the palette validator in both modes on land and ocean; on a stale clock every band in view is pale and the legend says nothing is newer than the snapshot date; URL shade=evidence reproduces the view and is never stored; no new banned word in the DOM.

items.title: Patterns alongside colour
items.summary: Textures, not only hue, carry meaning on the map: the coverage-gap hatch today; two-tone dots for UCDP conflict locations once conflict records are published; and, in the opt-in Kind shading, lines for civil unrest and dots for armed conflict beside their validated hues. Legend swatches, high-contrast mode and print use the same textures. On the deployed site only the gap hatch is visible yet.
items.acceptance: Gap hatch and conflict dots differ in geometry; one of the two dot inks clears 3:1 on every fill in both modes; distinct under simulated protanopia and deuteranopia, in forced-colours mode and in a grayscale print; every pattern has a legend row; no texture on cards; the conflict dots are exercised by the labelled test fixture, not by published data, until armed-conflict-context-layer unblocks.

items.title: A kind on every record, set by the pipeline
items.summary: Every record states its kind. The 84 existing records are 'collective action', the research contract's own term, with the basis recorded; nothing is guessed from titles or tags.
items.acceptance: kind and kind_basis on all records; the validator rejects a non-default kind without an event-local source; filter and badge appear only when more than one kind exists; the frozen 2 Oct fixture is untouched and a new kind fixture pins the literals.

items.title: Protest, strike and civil unrest from a re-read source
items.summary: A record becomes a protest, a strike, or civil unrest only after an agent re-reads the cited source and records its own words, including who the source says did what.
items.blocked_by: The research environment cannot open news websites, so no cited source can be re-read. Needs the same access as adding reports (a fetch-capable connector or a network allowlist for news domains).
items.acceptance: Each re-typed record cites the re-read source; 'civil unrest' requires the source's own attribution of violence to participants; no record is re-typed from its title, id or tags; the 18 keyword matches stay 'collective action' until re-read.

items.title: Offline ingest, validator and publish step for UCDP conflict data
items.summary: Scripts turn downloaded UCDP files into a separate conflict dataset with parties, years, and best, low and high death estimates; a validator refuses coordinates, individuals, single death figures and any status, score or trend field; a publish step applies the gate review.
items.acceptance: scripts/ingest_ucdp.py runs from local CSVs without network; scripts/validate_conflicts.py enforces the exact keys and refusals of the 4.1 spec; scripts/publish_conflicts.py refuses a failed gate; labelled synthetic fixtures exercise all three; the build allowlist and test_pipeline know the optional file.

items.title: Armed conflict as a re-published UCDP context layer
items.summary: Countries UCDP lists as conflict locations are dotted on the map and each conflict has a record with UCDP's parties, years and death estimates with bounds. It is context, not Protest Atlas research, and not a front-line map or a rating of how serious a conflict is.
items.blocked_by: This environment cannot reach ucdp.uu.se or ucdpapi.pcr.uu.se, and the UCDP licence and citation have not been read on the download page. Needs the data session with network access to UCDP hosts, the terms read on the page, and a gate-reviewed candidates file.
items.acceptance: Records pass the validator; licence and citation come from the downloaded terms; the window states years and provisional months actually present; every death figure carries low and high bounds, a year and a version; no 'ongoing', no coordinates, no score; the empty state shows until the file exists.

items.title: Comment stripping for scripts at build time
items.summary: Scripts ship with their contract comments (about 14 KB gzip). A tokenizer-based tool, not a regular expression, would strip them at build time and the budget test would measure the served output.
items.acceptance: A tokenizer-based stripper with a test run against the built output; template literals and regular-expression literals untouched; the budget test measures scripts as served; ceilings unchanged.
